newsitem.title: TUNISIA: PLO welcomes Libya's move on stranded Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: PLO welcomes Libya's move on stranded Palestinians.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) welcomed on Wednesday a decision by Libya to let back into its territory some 270 Palestinians stranded for more than year on the border with Egypt.

Palestinians have been stranded in a desert camp since September 1995 when Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi ordered thousands of Palestinians to go home, a move inspired by his campaign against the Palestinian peace accords with Israel.
But Libya changed its policy on Tuesday.

"We appreciate this positive step by the People's Committees and the Libyan leadership asking these people to return to Libya and resume their activities," a spokesman for the Palestinian embassy in Tripoli told Reuters.
He said 270 were still stuck on the border and he could not confirm that they had started moving back into Libya.
Libya said its expulsion of Palestinians was aimed at underlining Israel's control over access to Palestinian territories despite its peace accord on self-rule for the PLO.

Most Palestinians forced from Libya went to countries beyond Egypt but Egypt refused to admit those who had no proof they could continue to another country and they were left stranded at the border in miserable conditions.
